narrative.overview: DIA is a voice-first autonomous business teammate for small merchants, and its interface is the red-cloth bahi-khata opened on the counter under one lamp. The ground is a dark espresso desk; the content lives on warm cream paper panels; a red margin line runs through the page; type is ink-black; totals are gold. The merchant reads it the way they read a ledger, line by line, and DIA writes each agent step as a line being posted. There is no generic admin dashboard and no dark-cyber AI look: no glass, no gradients, no neon, no purple. Depth comes from the paper panel resting on the desk, not from blur or glow. Hierarchy is carried by weight and case, not by size alone, so the type scale stays narrow. Money and counts always use tabular numerals.
keyCharacteristics: Dark espresso desk ground (#0e0c0a) with warm cream paper panels (#f4ecdc) as the only content surface.
Red margin line (#b01e2a) used for primary actions, active navigation, pending approvals, and the margin rule.
Three text inks only: ink (#1a1612), ink-soft (#3a332a), and margin red for emphasis.
Gold (#b8860b) reserved for totals and the wordmark; never for body text.
Mukta for both Latin and Devanagari, weights 300-800; tabular numerals for all numbers.
Sharp corners (2px) everywhere except the fully round record button; stamps keep square corners.
One shadow only: the paper-panel drop; everything else is flat.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Body text on paper uses only Ink and Ink Soft; Margin Red is reserved for actions, status, and the margin line. Gold is an accent for totals and the wordmark, never for body text.

rules.name: The Margin Is Rare Rule
rules.body: The red margin is used on no more than one primary action and the active nav item per screen. Its rarity is what makes a stamp feel like a stamp.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: No glass, gradients, or neon anywhere. Depth comes from the paper panel resting on the desk ground, never from blur or glow.

rules.name: The Weight Carries Rank Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by weight and case, not by size alone; sizes stay within a narrow 10-24px band so the ledger stays compact.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every currency value and count uses tabular numerals via the .num utility. Never use proportional numerals for money.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Mukta is the only text face; Devanagari and Latin share one voice. Mono is reserved for code.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. The paper-panel shadow appears only on content surfaces (cards, message bubbles, preview panels). Nav, buttons, inputs, and chips are flat.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one shadow value in the system. Do not invent new elevations; if a surface needs separation, use a border or a tonal step instead.

rules.name: The Sharp Corners Rule
rules.body: 2px radius everywhere. Stamps and badges are square. Only the record button is round.

rules.name: The Thin Border Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px at low opacity (ink/10 on paper, white/5 on desk). A 2px border is reserved for stamps and pending-approval cards.

dos: Do use the espresso desk as the ground and cream paper as the only content surface.
Do keep Margin Red rare: one primary action and the active nav item per screen.
Do use Mukta for both Latin and Devanagari, and tabular numerals for all money and counts.
Do carry hierarchy with weight and case; keep sizes in the 10-24px band.
Do use the single paper-panel shadow for content surfaces; keep nav, buttons, inputs, and chips flat.
Do use 2px radius everywhere; square corners for stamps and badges.
Do use 1px ink/10 borders on paper and white/5 on desk; reserve 2px for stamps and pending-approval cards.
Do use the Margin Red 2px focus ring on every interactive element, with focus:outline-none.
Do keep the mobile bottom nav visible and clear it with bottom padding on main.
donts: Don't use glass, blur, gradients, or neon. Depth comes from the paper panel on the desk.
Don't introduce a second shadow or a new elevation level.
Don't use any typeface other than Mukta (and mono for code).
Don't use proportional numerals for money or counts.
Don't flood a screen with Margin Red; its rarity is the point.
Don't use rounded corners larger than 2px except the record button.
Don't add a multi-merchant switcher or template dashboard chrome; the UI is a single merchant's khata.
Don't fabricate metrics or numbers; every figure comes from the database or a tool result.
